title: FlightOption
description: A normalized, ranked flight candidate returned by search_flights (architecture.md §8). schema_version 1.1.0 (Checkpoint Phase 4 C.0, docs/adr/0009-phase4-checkpointc0-live-data-and-react-design.md) additively introduces optional 'flight_number', 'provider_reference', 'offer_expires_at', 'baggage_limitations', 'fare_limitations', 'duration_minutes', and 'legs' for connecting itineraries. Every existing 1.0.0 instance (none of the new fields set, single implicit leg) remains valid unchanged. This project never claims a seat is available now, a fare is guaranteed, an itinerary is booked, or that payment occurred -- a FlightOption is always a search-time snapshot (see FlightSearchResult.is_snapshot), never bookable inventory.

flight_number.description: 1.1.0+ only. Present only when the provider actually supplied a specific flight identifier -- never invented to fill this field.

duration_minutes.description: 1.1.0+ only. Total scheduled origin-to-destination duration. Independently derivable from depart_at/arrive_at; present explicitly so a caller never has to parse timestamps to rank by duration.

legs.description: 1.1.0+ only. Present only for connecting itineraries with more than one physical flight segment; a nonstop result omits this entirely (stops=0 is sufficient). Each leg is its own scheduled segment -- never a booking guarantee for any individual segment.

provider_reference.description: 1.1.0+ only. The provider's own opaque offer/quote identifier, if supplied -- never fabricated when absent.

offer_expires_at.description: 1.1.0+ only. When the provider states this quoted price/offer is no longer expected to be valid. Absence does not imply the offer is guaranteed indefinitely -- see FlightSearchResult.is_snapshot.

baggage_limitations.description: 1.1.0+ only. Free-text baggage allowance/restriction summary, present only when the provider actually supplied it.

fare_limitations.description: 1.1.0+ only. Free-text fare-rule summary (change/refund restrictions etc.), present only when the provider actually supplied it.
